Full four-endpoint suite under official IDs (wan2.7-t2v, wan2.7-i2v, wan2.7-r2v, wan2.7-videoedit): text-to-video, image-to-video with first/last-frame lock and continuation, reference-to-video with up to 5 reference images, and prompt-guided editing of existing footage. 2-15s at 720p/1080p, native audio in the same pass, precise color control (HEX codes and palettes) and strong character consistency across references.

models.est_cost_credits: Bundled with paid Gemini plans (daily song allowances by tier) and in preview on Vertex AI; no per-track rate captured, verify live.
models.strength: Google DeepMind's music model (Mar 25, 2026, announced on Google's own blog): up to 3-minute tracks at 48kHz with structural awareness, so a brief can name the intro, verse, chorus, and bridge and the model follows the map; vocals and instrumentals, lyrics in several languages, automatic cover art, and a SynthID watermark on every output. Available in the Gemini app, AI Studio, the Gemini API, Vertex AI (preview), Google Vids, and ProducerAI.
models.weakness: A shorter ceiling than Suno's song lengths and no stem-editing studio of its own; commercial-use terms for film work need a live check before release.
models.what_changed: NEW, added 2026-10-15 (completeness wave): the first Google audio record in the guide. Lyria 3 (Feb 2026) made 30-second clips; Pro is the version a filmmaker can actually score with.

models.best_use: The final mile: upscale finished AI clips to 4K delivery, rescue a soft hero shot, and add interpolated slow motion without re-generating
models.est_cost_credits: Astra Standard $19/mo promotional ($39 list) with 400 credits/mo (about 10 minutes of HD video); extra credits $0.10 each; also inside Topaz Studio at $34/mo; verify live (Topaz Labs pricing page, read Oct 2026).
models.strength: Topaz Labs' creative video upscaler, built specifically for AI-generated footage: Precise mode restores faithfully on its Starlight model, Creative mode imagines new detail at subtle or bold strength, Astra 2 (Apr 2026) added promptable upscaling with creativity and sharpness controls, and frame interpolation reaches 120fps and 8x slow motion. Output to 4K. Also reachable inside Adobe Firefly and Premiere.
models.weakness: Creative mode invents detail, which can change faces and text, so hero shots get a frame-by-frame check after upscaling; cloud credits meter long runtimes quickly; Adobe announced an acquisition of Topaz Labs in June 2026 (reported), so plan names may move, verify live.
models.what_changed: NEW, added 2026-10-15 (completeness wave): the guide's only upscaling guidance was a short decision skill and no upscaler had a record, while its delivery chapters assume a 4K finish. Typed suite, like Mirage Tesseract, because it is a finishing tool, not a shot generator.

models.strength: Performance capture without a stage: shoot a driving performance on any camera, give Act-Two a character image or video, and it transfers the performance onto the character, facial expressions, head rotation, hand gestures and full-body movement. With image inputs a gesture-control setting decides how much hand and body motion carries over, and environmental motion is synthesised so the character sits inside the scene instead of floating on it. Up to 30s at 24 fps, the clip lengths working scenes actually need.
models.est_cost_credits: About $0.05/s at Runway's API credit price ($0.01 per credit): Act-Two bills 5 credits per second of output, 3s minimum, on Runway plans and Runway Dev. MuAPI lists performance transfer at $0.07 per generation. Verify live.
models.weakness: One performer per pass, and the driving video needs a clearly visible face with no cuts; the performance you get is the performance you shot, it cannot invent acting. Output resolution sits below the current generation flagships, and it is a transfer tool, not a generator: no scene exists until a generator or a camera makes one.
models.best_use: Acted scenes with generated characters: direct the performance yourself on camera, then put it on any character. The fastest route to expressive, repeatable acting in AI film, and the standard fix for the dead faces pure text-to-video still produces.
models.what_changed: NEW, added 2026-10-15 (completeness coordinator addendum): a standing Runway first-party model (Runway Dev's proprietary line is Gen-4.5, Aleph 2.0 and Act-Two) that no lane of the completeness wave carried, despite performance capture being a core AI-film technique with its own skill family in this guide. Specs and rate verified against October 2026 guide coverage on 2026-10-15.
